Provenance of a query's result

Source: R/provenance.R
og_provenance.Rd

og_provenance(x) says how x was produced: the call, the Store Releases that answered, the Job ids, and the counts, including whether limit cut any off (total, truncated). A Local Source runs no Jobs: its answers record no Job ids, and no cost estimate.

Usage

og_provenance(x)

Arguments

x

A data frame returned by a query function such as og_tophits().

Value

A list of class og_provenance:

  • query: the call and its arguments, as text; args: the arguments as a list.

  • store_releases: the Store Releases that answered, as <store_id>/<release_id>.

  • job_ids: the API's Job ids (none for what a Local Source answered); existing: whether the API reattached you to a Job it already had.

  • cost_estimate: the API's cost estimate for the Jobs, summed.

  • total, truncated: how many Associations matched (what the API counted), and whether limit cut any off; returned: the rows of x.

  • retrieved: when the answer was read, as a POSIXct.

  • Clumped results: clump, a data frame with one row per Analysis clumped (one row, id NA, for og_clump() of one set): id, ld, ld_choice, r2, kb, and the API's counts hits (the variants clumped), absent (those not in the LD Store) and leads (index variants), and clumps: "computed" (clumped on the fly, as every clumping is today) or, once Store Releases carry them, "stored". ld_from says where the LD came from: "source" (the Source's LD resource) or "ancestry" (each Analysis's Assigned Ancestry, on an API Source with none).

  • LD results: ld, ld_choice, ld_from (as above) and absent (see og_ld_matrix()). og_clump() of Analyses matched to several LD Stores gives each in ld, and how each was chosen in ld_choice, one for one.

A data frame whose provenance was dropped (by merge(), say) raises an error of class opengwasr_no_provenance; one whose rows changed after rbind() or subsetting keeps a stale attribute, and gives the opengwasr_provenance_stale warning and NULL.

Details

It is attached to the data frame a query function returns, and describes exactly those rows. After you rbind() or subset the rows they are no longer what the query returned: the attribute may survive, but og_provenance() then warns (class opengwasr_provenance_stale) and returns NULL rather than give counts that no longer fit. Some operations, such as merge(), drop the attribute altogether, and og_provenance() then stops with class opengwasr_no_provenance. Keep it, or its counts, before you combine data frames. Adding columns doesn't matter. Every Association also carries its own store_id and release_id.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
top <- og_tophits(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", clump = FALSE, limit = 3)
og_provenance(top)$truncated
} # }
